Ok, so here's a simple test. Jump start the car. Then turn everything - lights, heat, anything that uses electricity. Let it run. If it keeps running (and the lights don't dim or anything) then it's the battery/connections. A wire brush and some baking soda is a place to start. If the headlights dim and the car dies then it's the alternator. Couple hundred bucks from an auto parts store and maybe an hour of time with a few metric sockets.

If you have a digital meter you can check more accurately. When the car is running check the voltage across the battery terminals. If it reads something like 13 -14 volts your alternator is good and your battery is bad. If it reads 12 volts or less while running your alternator is bad.

Also many chain auto parts store so will test you battery and charging system for you.

Do you have access to a multi-meter or just a DC voltage meter? A great battery will read about 12.4V, with the car running it should read about 14.5V. If you can get it running and it isn't above ~12V most likely it is the alternator.

It could also be the starter. One way to get a little more life out of a starter is to tap on it with a hammer. The starter is a bit harder to replace but the starter, alternator, and battery are very doable repairs for average people.

This time of year though, the change in temperatures will usually kill a weak battery. My money would be on the that. If you try a jump start, let the vehicle giving you a start run for a bit around 2,000-3,000 rpm in neutral. This will hopefully charge the weak battery a bit so when you go to try to start the Lincoln there is a little more charge in the weak battery.
